project.name: AgenticOS
project.description: Local-first AI operating system for agentic workflows. It coordinates model providers, skill templates, local vault memory, approval gates, integrations, routines, terminal sessions, MCP servers, and durable markdown artifacts.
project.mainGoal: A local-first command center for agentic workflows with shared memory, run history, approval gates, provider selection, social/research dashboards, and vault-backed artifacts.

architectureDecisions.evidence: README.md and agenticos.config.ts place vault and SQLite under the local workspace by default.
architectureDecisions.tradeoff: Fast local iteration and private artifacts, but multi-user, serverless, backup, and concurrency require a separate production persistence plan.

architectureDecisions.evidence: data/seed-integrations.ts seeds many mock integrations; lib/integrations/adapters.ts returns mock adapters.
architectureDecisions.tradeoff: UI and workflows stay usable without credentials, but real write/read semantics are not implemented for most adapters.

architectureDecisions.evidence: lib/agent/engine.ts writes final output through writeVaultMarkdown and indexes it through indexGeneratedArtifact.
architectureDecisions.tradeoff: Outputs survive sessions and can feed memory, but vault scans can become expensive without caching/index invalidation.

architectureDecisions.decision: Provider abstraction around model endpoints and CLIs
architectureDecisions.tradeoff: Simple provider switching, but provider-specific payloads, model catalogs, costs, and failure modes are hardcoded.

architectureDecisions.decision: Approval gate modeled as persisted request records
architectureDecisions.tradeoff: Clear audit surface, but approval status is not connected to a resumable executor.
Provider-agnostic behavior is easy to edit/version, but context size is clipped and no semantic retrieval is used.

constraints.description: Filesystem, child_process, node-pty, SQL.js, and node-cron require Node runtime. Edge runtime is not viable for core routes.
Runtime assumes local disk access to vault/ and .agenticos/. Deploying to serverless without mounted persistent disk loses state or breaks features.
No authentication, authorization, CSRF, tenancy, or rate limits are present in the inspected API routes, including process-spawning terminal/MCP/test routes.
Project instructions require approval before risky external actions; current implementation persists approvals but does not resume gated execution.
The SQLite database is held as a singleton in memory and exported to disk after writes; safe only for single-process local use.
Vault and test source folders are untracked at final validation. A clean clone with tracked files only will miss imported modules and the test runner.

architecturalIssues.title: Important source folders are untracked and must be committed with the .gitignore fix
evidence: git status shows app/api/vault, app/vault, components/vault, lib/vault, app/api/tests, app/tests, components/tests, tests, and vitest.config.ts as untracked
architecturalIssues.impact: A clean clone or CI build from tracked files only will miss the vault implementation, test runner, and unit tests. If the .gitignore fix is not committed with these files, the earlier nested-vault ignore problem can reappear.
architecturalIssues.recommendation: Commit the `.gitignore` `/vault/` change together with the vault source folders, test source folders, tests, and vitest.config.ts.

architecturalIssues.title: Unauthenticated terminal, MCP, test runner, vault, scheduler, approval, and run mutation APIs
architecturalIssues.impact: If reachable beyond a trusted local browser, an attacker can start a shell/CLI, run npm tests as a child process, send raw input, spawn arbitrary MCP commands, mutate vault files, start workflows, and change approvals.
architecturalIssues.recommendation: Keep these routes localhost-only during development. Before any hosted use, add authentication, CSRF protection, authorization checks, request audit context, and explicit command allowlists.

architecturalIssues.title: Background run execution is tied to the API route process lifetime
architecturalIssues.impact: Long model calls can be killed when the request/runtime instance ends, especially on serverless platforms. Runs may remain stuck in planning or partial states.
architecturalIssues.recommendation: Move execution to a real worker/queue with durable jobs, heartbeats, retries, cancellation, and explicit run lease ownership.

architecturalIssues.title: SQL.js persistence is single-process and save-on-every-write
architecturalIssues.impact: Concurrent API calls can interleave writes or lose data. Multi-process dev/serverless deployments can diverge because each process owns a separate in-memory Database instance.
architecturalIssues.recommendation: For production, move to a real SQLite driver with WAL/locking or a hosted database. For local-only, serialize writes through a mutex and batch save operations.

architecturalIssues.title: Approval status updates do not resume or execute blocked work
architecturalIssues.impact: The UI can approve/reject records, but there is no executor that consumes approved requests and performs the originally blocked tool call. Approval is currently an audit/status concept, not an action gate.
architecturalIssues.recommendation: Model gated tool calls as resumable jobs with exact payloads, idempotency keys, post-approval execution handlers, and post-execution audit records.

architecturalIssues.title: Scheduler and vault indexing start from root layout module side effects
architecturalIssues.impact: Next module loading, dev HMR, multiple workers, or serverless cold starts can start duplicate schedulers or expensive vault walks at unpredictable times.
architecturalIssues.recommendation: Move startup work behind an explicit singleton service, a CLI/dev command, or a dedicated worker process.

architecturalIssues.title: Most integrations remain mock-first while UI labels suggest broad operational coverage
evidence: README.md moving from mock mode section
architecturalIssues.impact: Product capability can be overestimated. Only selected read paths are live: YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Hacker News, GitHub Trending, provider checks, terminal/CLI, MCP registration.
architecturalIssues.recommendation: Add capability flags per action and distinguish UI copy between live, mock, read-only, draft-only, and approval-gated write support.

architecturalIssues.title: Several source files contain mojibake in UI strings and generated markdown text
evidence: Observed sequences like `â€”`, `Â·`, `â†’`, `â€¦` in app, lib, and component output
architecturalIssues.impact: Users will see corrupted punctuation in UI, vault artifacts, SSE output, and generated summaries.
architecturalIssues.recommendation: Normalize source files to UTF-8 and replace corrupted sequences with correct characters or ASCII-safe equivalents.

architecturalIssues.title: GitHub Trending integration scrapes HTML with regex
architecturalIssues.impact: GitHub markup changes can break the research panel without a typed failure mode.
architecturalIssues.recommendation: Prefer an official API where possible, or isolate parser tests with saved fixtures and observable error reporting.

recommendedNextActions.action: Commit the current `.gitignore` `/vault/` fix together with untracked vault/test source folders and vitest.config.ts.
Add auth/localhost binding and command allowlists before exposing API routes to any network.
Move run execution and scheduler work into a durable worker/queue model.
Replace SQL.js save-on-every-write with a persistence strategy that has locking, migrations, backups, and concurrency guarantees.
